What US and EU copy usually gets wrong for China

  • Literal subtitle translation — English slogans become stiff zh-Hans that waste the 30-character subtitle limit
  • Keyword field copied from English — the 100-character field needs Mainland search terms, not comma-split en-US nouns
  • Description opens with feature bullets — China skim readers expect a clear outcome in the first line, not a settings-menu dump
  • Traditional characters or Taiwan phrasing — zh-Hans for mainland requires Simplified script and local word choice
  • Untranslated screenshots — store copy in Chinese while galleries stay English signals an unfinished launch
  • Superlatives without local proof — “#1,” “best,” and press quotes from US pages rarely belong unchanged on CN listings

Simplified Chinese field limits (verify in Connect)

  • Title — brand plus category noun; avoid pinyin-only names unless people search that way in China
  • Subtitle — one new fact (audience, workflow, pricing); not a second keyword dump
  • Keywords — 100 characters, comma-separated, no spaces after commas; synonyms and problem phrases not already visible
  • Description — lead with who the app is for and the primary outcome; align meaning with en-US without identical sentence structure
